_comment: Hand-maintained register of every tracked exception/finding this repository carries, cross-referenced with the machine-generated secreport.json/vex.json (cmd/secreport). Update this file in the same PR that changes an exception's scope or review date.

entries.title: 5 remaining npm audit findings (low only) in website/ (Docusaurus dev-tooling deps) -- reduced from 26 on 2026-11-14
entries.affected_component: website/package-lock.json: deepmerge, @svgr/plugin-svgo, @svgr/webpack, @docusaurus/plugin-svgr, @docusaurus/preset-classic (SVG-handling chain only -- tinypool, webpack-dev-server/sockjs/uuid, serialize-javascript, copy-webpack-plugin, and css-minimizer-webpack-plugin were fixed, see remediation)
entries.fixed_version: none safe for the remaining 5 -- deepmerge has no patched release at all (its vulnerable range >=4.2.0 covers every version up to and including the latest, 4.3.1, confirmed via `npm view deepmerge versions`); npm's only suggested fix for the rest of the chain is `--force`-installing an OLDER @docusaurus/preset-classic (3.6.3, a downgrade from the pinned 3.10.2, isSemVerMajor: true), rejected for the same reason as the original investigation
entries.exploitability_context: build/dev-tooling only (npm start, docusaurus build) -- none of the affected packages ship in website/build/, the deployed static site. Stronger evidence as of 2026-11-14: @svgr/plugin-svgo@8.1.0's actual compiled code (node_modules/@svgr/plugin-svgo/dist/index.js) never calls deepmerge at all, despite declaring it as a package.json dependency -- confirmed by direct inspection, not assumed. The vulnerable mergeObject() function is not reachable through this installed version's real code path, on top of being build-time-only
entries.environment: local development and CI build tooling, not the published site
entries.remediation: 2026-11-14: fixed 21 of 26 findings (including all 16 critical and the 1 high) via three targeted package.json `overrides` -- tinypool (1.1.1 -> 2.2.0), serialize-javascript (6.0.2 -> 7.1.4), uuid (8.3.2 -> 11.1.1) -- verified compatible (npm install + docusaurus build + link check all pass unchanged, no --force used). The remaining 5 (deepmerge and its dependents, all low severity) were re-investigated the same day for every option short of a major migration: (1) upgrade -- impossible, deepmerge has no patched release at all (its vulnerable range >=4.2.0 covers every published version through the latest, 4.3.1, confirmed via `npm view deepmerge versions`); (2) a supported framework config (`svgr: false` in preset-classic's options, a real, documented option -- confirmed in node_modules/@docusaurus/preset-classic/lib/index.js) -- tested and rejected: it stops Docusaurus from *using* @docusaurus/plugin-svgr, but does not remove it from node_modules/package-lock.json, since it's a hard (non-optional) dependency declared in @docusaurus/preset-classic's own package.json -- `npm audit`'s finding count is unchanged by this flag; (3) replacement -- no npm mechanism exists to swap one package name for another inside a third party's dependency tree (overrides only repin versions of the same name), and patching @svgr's source directly (e.g. via patch-package) was judged a disproportionate maintenance burden for a LOW-severity, non-reachable, build-time-only finding. Next real step, if ever warranted: a dedicated Docusaurus major-version migration, as its own reviewable change
entries.status: open, tracked. Closed and reopened twice on 2026-11-13, each time without a linked remediation PR: first closed ~12:45, reopened ~13:03 after re-verification (live CI re-check, PR #45: 26 findings, matching this entry's then-current severity breakdown); closed again ~18:41, reopened again after a second re-verification (fresh npm audit: still 26 findings, identical breakdown both times). The count above (5, all low) reflects a REAL fix applied 2026-11-14 (see remediation), not a change in issue-tracker state -- website/.security/npm-audit-baseline.json has been updated to this new baseline and still gates on it in CI. This status is not a claim that the remaining 5 are resolved.

entries.title: Python base-image OS-package CVEs -- 0 findings of ANY severity as of 2026-11-14 (was 98 HIGH/CRITICAL)
entries.affected_component: apps/python-api's runtime image base -- moved python:3.12-slim-bookworm -> python:3.12-slim-trixie -> python:3.12-alpine across this investigation (2026-11-14)
entries.fixed_version: krb5-libs 1.22.3-r0 and zlib 1.4-r0 (both applied, cleared the base image's 16 HIGH findings); pip's own package metadata (5 MEDIUM, 1 LOW) removed from the image entirely (not just the console-script binary -- its dist-info in site-packages too)
entries.exploitability_context: No findings of any severity remain to assess reachability for
entries.evidence: fully unfiltered Trivy scan (no severity filter at all, not just HIGH/CRITICAL) against the final built image: zero findings. Reproducible via `trivy image <image>` -- the CI gate (`ignore-unfixed` exception removed entirely, see python-ci.yml) runs at the full HIGH,CRITICAL threshold with nothing suppressed, and nothing beyond that threshold remains either
entries.remediation: 2026-11-14, four steps, each verified compatible before switching (full test suite, ruff, mypy, a real build/run, /healthz unchanged at every step): (1) bookworm -> trixie: 98 findings (2 critical) -> 47 (0 critical). (2) trixie -> alpine: re-tested the F3 distroless/Alpine rejection (docs/adr/0004) -- musllinux wheels now exist on PyPI for pydantic_core/uvloop/httptools/watchfiles (none existed when F3 rejected this), so no compiler is needed; base-image findings dropped to 16 HIGH, 0 critical. (3) `apk upgrade krb5-libs=1.22.3-r0 zlib=1.4-r0` cleared all 16, leaving 5 MEDIUM/1 LOW, all pip's own package metadata (not a runtime dependency; the console-script binary was already excluded, but its dist-info in site-packages lingered). (4) `rm -rf` pip's package directory and dist-info from the final image, after the builder-stage copy (removing it before the copy would just have it reintroduced, since the builder's own site-packages -- itself based on the same python:3.12-alpine image -- has it too). Confirmed via a fully unfiltered scan: zero findings remain.
entries.status: fully resolved as of 2026-11-14 (0 findings of any severity, down from 98 HIGH/CRITICAL) -- the GitHub issue itself has not been closed by this change; that is a separate decision requiring explicit approval, not made here. Prior history: closed and reopened twice on 2026-11-13, each time without a linked remediation PR, after re-verification showed the then-current 98 findings still present both times. This entry's prior reductions (98 -> 47 trixie, -> 0 HIGH/CRITICAL alpine) are superseded by this one (-> 0 of any severity); nothing about any prior record is deleted, only superseded by a later, more complete fix.
